text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOMATED PAGE fired (PD: #INC-47821) — multiple regions reporting edge 5xx/TLS handshake failures, LB target flapping. Priority: P1.

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification: INC-47821 created and sent to @mike-oncall (primary).

mike-oncall: acked. see if this is a regression from the recent config push? pulling up graphs now.

janelle-sre: copying perf dash — eu-west shows spike in 503 rates starting ~+00:03. tls handshakes failing with `tls: unexpected message` in nginx logs.

marco-network: seeing a correlated surge of NXDOMAIN and stale answers from several DNS caches in front of our edge. Some resolvers returning old CNAME that points to retired lb-targets. TTLs look low, but caches upstream appear sticky.

sara-ops: customer-impact: 12% of requests fail in EU, APAC partial degradation, US mostly green. Reporting from one customer (cs-tilly) with enterprise traffic — they see ~20% error rate.

cs-tilly: confirmed — widgets failing intermittently, timeouts then TLS alerts in browser console. Hold on while we route around.

mike-oncall: OK, can we confirm whether this is DNS or LB health? health checks for the flagged targets show healthy afterwards, but LB still draining in some azs. possible cached DNS pointing at retired targets causing handshake mismatch.

janelle-sre: pulled a sample of failing client IPs. When resolving, their resolver returns CNAME -> retired-edge-02.redwood.net for ~30% of lookups. retired-edge-02 has expired cert (rotation stepped down last week) — handshake fails. That explains TLS errors immediately.

marco-network: yup — upstream ISP resolvers are returning cached entries even though origin changed. Looks like a 'tainted cache' situation. Because our incident-bot has a low-repeat backoff, PD keeps re-firing as more symptomatic requests hit those caches -> pagerloop. we need to stop noisy pages and mitigate customer impact.

mike-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) suppress automated re-page for this PD while we triage (can we set PD auto-escalation backoff?). 2) issue DNS emergency TTL override / serve negative cache-control via our authoritative DNS to force revalidate. 3) put a temporary traffic weight shift away from retired-edge-02 in the LB. 4) contact large affected customers with temporary workarounds.

pagerduty: auto-escalation paused for INC-47821 by @mike-oncall at +00:12. acknowledgement recorded.

janelle-sre: executing failover playbook:
```
# set low TTL on authoritative zone
cli> r53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"redwood.net.","Type":"CNAME","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"edge-alias.redwood.net."}]}}]}'
```

marco-network: pushed TTL 30s to authoritative. propagation shows authoritative servers updated. but many public caches will honor older TTL until expiry.

mike-oncall: performing weight shift on LB — move traffic off retired-edge-02 by setting weight=0 for that target in eu-west pools.

janelle-sre: submitted LB update: retired-edge-02 weight -> 0. health check still reports green but we'll drain for safety.

sara-ops: staging a customer-facing alert: "We are investigating intermittent errors in EU/APAC due to DNS cache inconsistency. Mitigations underway: low TTL, LB weight shift, contacting affected customers." Want to push to status page now?

cs-tilly: please do, our support window is filling up. thanks.

mike-oncall: pushing status update.

incident-bot: System note: change detected — LB weight update by janelle-sre.

janelle-sre: logs after weight shift look better for requests hitting updated resolvers. But some client resolvers still resolving to retired-edge-02 until their TTL expires (could be up to previous TTL ~300s). CC: PD still shows multiple duplicate alerts coming from edge-proxy healthcheck because probes are hitting retired hosts.

marco-network: next step — contact major resolver partners (ISP peering contacts) and request cache flush where possible. Also we can temporarily create a redirect on retired-edge-02 that answers TLS with proper cert and proxies traffic to healthy backends to reduce customer impact while TTLs stale. Risky but low change surface. Thoughts?

mike-oncall: prefer airy approach: if we can hotfix retired-edge-02 to present the current cert and route to healthy backends, that would quickly reduce TLS failures. Do it only if it's quick (<10m) and fully reversible.

janelle-sre: implementing cert reload and proxy rule. follow commands:
```
ssh retired-edge-02
sudo cp /run/certs/current.pem /etc/nginx/certs/fullchain.pem
sudo systemctl reload nginx
# add proxy-pass to healthy pool
```

marco-network: confirming retired-edge-02 now serves new cert; tcpdump shows handshakes succeed from test clients. Great.

sara-ops: error rate dropping in eu-west: from 12% -> 3% over last 5 mins. APAC improving too. Notified top 3 affected customers.

pagerduty: Following suppression, no new escalations. PD incident now in maintenance window controlled by @mike-oncall.

mike-oncall: temporary mitigations applied. next actions: follow up task to purge stale cache signals with resolver partners, monitor for recurrence, and run RCA after full recovery. I'm handing off to @janelle-sre for postmortem and long-term fixes.

janelle-sre: handover ACK. capturing timeline and adding action items: - audit DNS change process for retired targets; - add guardrails to auto-decommission paths so certs aren't removed before DNS fully drained; - improve incident-bot dedupe to detect repeated alerts from known-tainted-cache patterns and backoff.

cs-tilly: thanks for the quick response team. we'll validate on our side and reopen if we see more issues.

mike-oncall: closing active page loop. setting follow-up meeting in 30m to review mitigation and customer comms. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Note: INC-47821 status -> stabilized. auto-pages resumed under normal policy at +00:45.
